name: Sodium bicarbonate
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Sodium bicarbonate is an alkalinizing agent; the bicarbonate is handled by the kidney and lungs, so there is no kidney dose reduction. The kidney concern is the sodium load: the US label (isotonic IV solution) asks for monitoring for fluid overload in kidney disease and anuria, plus electrolytes to avoid alkalosis and hypernatremia. Oral tablets used for the metabolic acidosis of CKD are outside this label.
kidney_function_basis: Not applicable: dosing is by acid-base status, not kidney function.

bands.recommendation: IV for metabolic acidosis (adults and children 2 years and older): 2 to 5 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours, by bicarbonate, total CO2, pH and clinical state (label). Treat the cause.

No kidney dose change in the label. Kidney disease and anuria increase sensitivity to the sodium load: watch for fluid overload, edema and blood pressure, and adjust other sodium sources (label 5.1). Monitor bicarbonate, sodium and potassium; avoid overshoot alkalosis.

hd: No dose change; anuria raises the risk of fluid overload from the sodium load (label 5.1). Dialysate bicarbonate also corrects acidosis; coordinate with the dialysis prescription (clinical judgment).
pd: No dose change; watch sodium load and fluid status (label 5.1).
crrt: No data in label. CRRT fluids are usually bicarbonate-buffered; added IV bicarbonate is a specialist decision guided by blood gases.
dialyzable: Bicarbonate crosses dialysis membranes in both directions according to the dialysate bicarbonate concentration (physiology; not stated in label).
monitoring: Blood gases or serum bicarbonate, sodium, potassium (hypokalemia as acidosis corrects), fluid status, blood pressure, edema. Extravasation site (hypertonic solutions).

pediatric.usual_dose: 2 years and older: 2 to 5 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours. Under 2 years and neonates: 1 to 2 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours; avoid rapid or bolus doses (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Under 2 years: rate no more than 8 mEq/kg/day (label 8.4).
pediatric.neonates: 1 to 2 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours; no more than 8 mEq/kg/day; rapid injection risks hypernatremia and intracranial hemorrhage (label).

renal.recommendation: No dose change; watch sodium load and fluid status (label 5.1).

adult: Selected US label is an isotonic 1.26% (0.150 mEq/mL) premixed bag (Baxter, 2026). PH registers 8.4% (1 mEq/mL) ampoules/vials (38 products) and 325 or 650 mg tablets (29). The 8.4% hypertonic solution carries more extravasation and hypernatremia risk; consider pinning an 8.4% US label as an alternate.

Oral sodium bicarbonate for CKD metabolic acidosis (KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline) is not covered by this label; guideline thresholds were not read for this batch, so none are stated. Dr. Rivero to decide whether to add a KDIGO line.
Dialyzability line is general physiology, labelled as such.
